question.problem: A triangle $△LMN$ has $m∠L={90}^{∘},$ $m∠N={37}^{∘},$ and $LM=8.$ Find the length of $\overset{―}{LN}$ rounded to the nearest integer.
question.worked_solution:
For an angle $\theta $ in a right triangle, the trigonometric ratios are as follows:

- $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{opposite leg}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$

- $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{adjacent leg}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$

- $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{opposite leg}}{\text{adjacent leg}}$

First, let's sketch the given triangle.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14228914/assets/38dcba98867c158c671b35ec033fa1ec55c8cedc67466ebe981de9fbbae314e9.png)

Notice that we are given the length of the leg $\overset{―}{LM}$ opposite to the given angle $∠N$ and wish to find the length of the leg $\overset{―}{LN}$ adjacent$∠N.$

The trigonometric ratio that relates the opposite leg to the adjacent leg is *tangent*. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠N) & =\frac{\text{opposite leg}}{\text{adjacent leg}} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡({37}^{∘}) & =\frac{8}{LN} \\ LN\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡({37}^{∘}) & =8 \\ LN & =\frac{8}{\operatorname{tan}⁡({37}^{∘})}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using a calculator to evaluate the trigonometric ratio, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}LN & =\frac{8}{\operatorname{tan}⁡({37}^{∘})} \\  & =\frac{8}{(0.753\,55…)} \\  & =10.616\,35… \\  & ≈11,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest integer.
